chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya from al-Abbas ibn Ma'ruf from Hammad ibn Isa from Ali ibn Abi Hamzah who said:

He was asked about a man who did not know how to perform Tawaf around the House until he returned to his family. He said: 'If it was due to ignorance, he must repeat the Hajj and upon him is a sacrificial animal (Badanah).'

key_terms.بَدَنَةٌ: a sacrificial camel (or cow/sheep depending on context, but specifically a large animal here)
key_terms.يَطُوفَ بِالْبَيْتِ: to perform Tawaf around the Kaaba

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a pilgrim who forgets or does not know how to perform Tawaf before leaving Mecca?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Shaykh al-Tusi records a ruling where ignorance of the obligation to perform Tawaf al-Ifadah necessitates repeating the entire Hajj and offering a *Badanah* (a camel or cow). This highlights the Shia juristic emphasis on the completeness of Hajj pillars, distinguishing between minor omissions and those requiring full repetition due to the fundamental nature of Tawaf as a core rite.
